correctness.rationale: The source paper's exact finite boundary reduction turns the count into a Bernoulli lattice probability. The normalized Gram matrix converges to G_k=k^{-1}I+(k+2)k^{-2}J, and linearly many standard-basis columns give full lattice span and exponential control away from the central Fourier saddle. Fourier inversion then yields the stated Gaussian local limit and closed leading constant; exact dynamic-programming counts support the algebra and constants.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 motivating preprint proves only two-sided order bounds for fixed discrepancy and does not state a leading constant, covariance/local-limit law, square-root-scale Gaussian profile, or exact asymptotic ratio across weights. Searches of synonymous formulations and related weighted-representation literature found no prior coverage. The 2012 Yang--Chen paper was not inspected in full, but the 2026 primary source describes its counting result as finiteness plus logarithmic growth; very recent unindexed follow-up remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The theorem converts a new order-of-magnitude counting result into an explicit sharp asymptotic, identifies the full multivariate Gaussian fluctuation profile, sharpens comparisons between different weights, and supplies the leading constant for the related Yan--Shan counting function.
